Chemical Properties: As stated earlier, Alkanes are chemically inactive to a great extent. So they do not react with acids, bases, oxidants or reductants. However, they take part in some chemical reactions.

**Reaction with Chlorine**

Tetrachloro Methane is produced when Chlorine is mixed with Methane in the presence of Ultra Violet (UV) light. This reaction is accomplished in four phases.

$$\text{CH}_4 + \text{Cl}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{UV}} \text{CH}_3\text{Cl} + \text{HCl}$$
$$\text{Methane} \quad \text{Chlorine} \quad \text{Chloro Methane} \quad \text{Hydrogen Chloride}$$

$$\text{CH}_3\text{Cl} + \text{Cl}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{UV}} \text{CH}_2\text{Cl}_2 + \text{HCl}$$
$$\text{Chloro Methane} \quad \text{Chlorine} \quad \text{Dichloro Methane} \quad \text{Hydrogen Chloride}$$

$$\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}_2 + \text{Cl}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{UV}} \text{CHCl}_3 + \text{HCl}$$
$$\text{Dichloro Methane} \quad \text{Chlorine} \quad \text{Trichloro Methane} \quad \text{Hydrogen Chloride}$$

$$\text{CHCl}_3 + \text{Cl}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{UV}} \text{CCl}_4 + \text{HCl}$$
$$\text{Trichloro Methane} \quad \text{Chlorine} \quad \text{Tetrachloro Methane} \quad \text{Hydrogen Chloride}$$

**Combustion Reaction with Oxygen:** Methane reacts with oxygen of air and thus carbon-di-oxide, water vapours and heat are produced. This heat is used in cooking.

$$\text{CH}_4 + 2\text{O}_2 \longrightarrow \text{CO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{Heat}$$
$$\text{Methane} \quad \text{Oxygen} \quad \text{Carbon-di-oxide} \quad \text{Water} \quad \text{Heat}$$
